CE N'EST PAS UN RECENSEMENT. La BRH agré: THIS IS NOT A CENSUS. The BRH licenses 58 credit unions and counts 108 service points; contributory mapping shows about thirty. An object is recognised either because its NAME declares it — « caisse populaire », « kès popilè », « CEC » — or because it carries an acronym licensed by the BRH AND is tagged as financial. A bare acronym is not enough: one of the licensed acronyms is the word « success », which would otherwise catch a school, a pharmacy and a water point. The rule therefore misses badly tagged credit unions, and that is the direction in which it must err. at2.bio: ATM — Andrelita T. Myril — is a painter and visual artist, a graduate of ENARTS, Haiti's most renowned National School of Arts. Her mission: put the tools of art in everyone's hands — to grow each person's creativity, give the mind the escape it needs, and nurture human and mental balance. Her canvases — bold colors, moving rhythms, figures and abstractions — are windows onto the light of Haiti and the Caribbean.
at2.com_desc: Portraits, landscapes, pieces for your home, office or event — tell us about your project and ATM will bring it to color.
at2.home_desc: The works of Andrelita T. Myril (ATM) become digital experiences: image, voice, clip, poster. Free to view and listen to; institutions fund access and prints for a community. Originals still available, price on request.
at2.kicker: Color, movement, light — art and creativity that let our minds breathe.

bia.eth1: Data literacy. I publish free tutorials — in Haitian Creole, French, English and Spanish — that teach how to read a figure, spot a bias and check a source. Training your teams is part of the job, not an after-sales extra.
bia.eth2: Ethics. A badly defined indicator steers a decision that affects real people. I name the biases, I document the limits, and I refuse conclusions the data does not support — including when they would suit everybody.
bia.eth3: Privacy. Personal data minimised, anonymised, explicit consent. In the recruiting portal I built, a candidate's contact stays hidden until they are selected, and nationality never appears in a browsing list — because the law and human dignity both require it.
bia.fq1_a: That is not the goal, and it is not what we sell. We look for the repetitive tasks that wear your teams out, and we explicitly protect those that require judgement and relationships. An honest diagnostic always states what must NOT be automated.
bia.fq2_a: We sign a confidentiality agreement before any access. The diagnostic sets a written rule on what must never enter an AI tool, and the pilot is designed to work with reduced or anonymised data wherever possible.
bia.fq3_a: That is a real risk and we put it in writing. Every automation ships with its known cost, a spending cap, and a documented manual fallback. You must never be locked in by a provider.
bia.fq3_q: What if the AI provider changes its prices or rules?
bia.fq4_a: Yes — and that is where the effect is strongest: one person recovering five hours a week, in a team of six, is visible. The diagnostic is fixed-price precisely to stay affordable.
bia.fq4_q: We are a small organisation. Is this for us?
bia.fq5_a: Two pilots in parallel, at most. We prefer to say so and keep an honest schedule rather than promise deadlines that quality could not survive.
bia.hw1: A 30-minute call. You describe your work, we say plainly whether AI can help — and if the answer is no, we say that too.
bia.hw2: Diagnostic. Interviews with your teams, observation of the real work, measurement of volumes. No technical decision at this stage.
bia.hw3: Findings workshop. Ninety minutes: the task map, the roadmap, the risks. You decide whether to continue, or you stop there.
bia.hw4: Pilot. A single task, taken through to live use, with your teams in the loop.
bia.hw5: Handover. Your team runs the tool without us. That is the success criterion — not our permanent presence.
bia.kicker: You want to use AI without betting your reputation on it.
bia.lead: Most AI engagements stop at the demo that impresses in a meeting. We don't deliver a demo, we deliver proof: an automation actually in service, traceable, tested, with a known cost — and a clear list of the tasks that must stay human.

Most monitoring-and-evaluation specialists do not build the tools they ask for; most developers have never had to defend an indicator in front of a donor. I have done both — which is why I know where automation holds, and where it breaks.

ds.prd026_p: Count of telecom equipment by commune, by operator and by kind — 498 items across 81 communes out of 140. A contributory count: it measures the mapping effort as much as the real network.
ds.prd027_meta: 💰 Economy • Sources : Banque mondiale — WDI ; OIT — ILOSTAT ; FAO — FAOSTAT ; UN Comtrade • confidence level A • CC BY 4.0 (Banque mondiale, OIT) ; CC BY 4.0 avec clause de non-promotion (FAO) ; conditions UNSD, agrégats transformés seulement (Comtrade)

They do NOT go down to the commune and must not: they serve as a yardstick for reading a local figure. ds.prd028_meta: 📄 Tourism • Sources : OpenStreetMap via HOT • confidence level C • ODbL
ds.prd028_p: Hotels, guest houses, sites, museums, viewpoints, campsites, tourist information, restaurants and bars mapped in OpenStreetMap, coloured by family — 2896 points across 115 of 140 communes. ds.prd029_meta: 📄 Tourism • Sources : OpenStreetMap via HOT • confidence level C • ODbL

ds.prd030_meta: 📄 Tourism • Sources : Ministère du Tourisme et des Industries créatives (MTIC) • confidence level B • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5 (textes officiels et simples données). Agrégat communal recalculé par Atmart.

What the ministry CLASSIFIED, not what exists — and nothing has succeeded this classification since 2015. ds.prd031_h: Consumer price index, by region and commune
ds.prd031_meta: 📄 Prices • Sources : IHSI — Institut Haïtien de Statistique et d'Informatique • confidence level B • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5 (textes officiels et simples données). Agrégat régional rattaché aux communes par Atmart.
ds.prd031_p: The IHSI consumer price index broken down into five regions and attached to the 140 communes: index level, monthly change and twelve-month change. This is the ONLY territorial granularity the Haitian price index has — no international source goes below the country. Warning: the 140 communes carry only FIVE distinct values, those of the regions. It is not a communal index, and it would be wrong to conclude that one commune is dearer than another within the same region. The annex gives the series of published months by region.
ds.prd032_meta: 📄 Prices • Sources : PAM (WFP) via OCHA HDX • confidence level B • CC BY-IGO 3.0
ds.prd032_p: The annual average price of seven staple foods across the nine markets monitored by WFP, in gourdes AND in dollars. THIS IS NOT A CONSUMER PRICE INDEX: only two staples are tracked throughout in all nine markets, and neither housing, nor transport, nor energy appears here. What this product shows and no national average reveals: the same marmite of maize meal costs 291 gourdes in Jérémie and 700 in Ouanaminthe on 2024 average. And over twenty years it is multiplied by 10.8 in gourdes but only 3.5 in dollars — the gap is the currency's depreciation.
ds.prd033_h: Licensed financial institutions, and what the map does not show
ds.prd033_meta: 🏛 Public finances • Sources : BRH — supervision bancaire ; OpenStreetMap via HOT • confidence level B • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5 (textes officiels et simples données)
ds.prd033_p: The 26 institutions licensed by the BRH — banks, money transfer houses, bureaux de change, electronic payment, microfinance — with their head office, set against the names recorded by contributory mapping. EIGHT licensed institutions are named by NO point on the map: three transfer houses, three bureaux de change, two electronic payment providers. That is the more useful half, because it says where to go and look. Order of magnitude to keep in mind: the BRH counts 5,250 financial service providers in June 2024; the contributory map carries 474.
ds.prd034_meta: 🏛 Public finances • Sources : BRH — liste des caisses populaires agréées • confidence level B • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5
ds.prd034_p: The 58 credit unions licensed by the BRH (March 2025 list): name, acronym, licence number, commune of the head office, number of counters, federation. This is the ONLY official financial list that reaches the territory — for banks and money transfer houses the BRH publishes the head office only. 57 of 58 unions are attached to a commune, across 47 communes. No telephone, no e-mail: a territorial atlas has no need of them.
ds.prd035_meta: 🏛 Public finances • Sources : OpenStreetMap via HOT ; sigles agréés de la BRH • confidence level C • ODbL
ds.prd035_p: The cooperative finance points recorded by OpenStreetMap, recognised one by one: 30 credit unions or cooperatives and 13 microfinance points, named and located, across 26 communes. THIS IS NOT A CENSUS — the BRH licenses 58 credit unions and counts 108 service points. An object is kept only if its name declares it or if it carries an acronym licensed by the BRH on an object tagged as financial: the rule misses badly tagged credit unions, and that is the direction in which it must err. Solidarity mutuals are not here and cannot be: without a licence, without premises, often without a stable name.
ds.prd036_h: The licence of every published file
ds.prd036_meta: 📐 Method • Sources : Registre des sources et passeports juridiques d'Atmart • confidence level A • CC BY 4.0
ds.prd036_p: One line per file on the site: its licence, the sources it comes from, the attribution to carry, and the reason. THERE IS NOT ONE LICENCE BUT SEVERAL, and that is the point: eleven files go out under ODbL because they derive from OpenStreetMap, whose share-alike passes to redistributed derived databases; others fall under no licence at all, since article 5 of the Haitian decree of 12 October 2005 excludes official texts and simple data from copyright. Announcing CC BY everywhere would grant a right the source withholds; announcing ODbL everywhere would forbid without cause. The table is recomputed from the source register at every run.
ds.prd037_h: The Haitian diaspora — where it lives
ds.prd037_meta: 👥 Population • Sources : ONU DESA — International Migrant Stock 2024 • confidence level A • CC BY 3.0 IGO
ds.prd037_p: How many people BORN IN HAITI live in each country, from 1990 to 2024, by sex. Two million in 2024 against 521,000 in 1990 — nearly four times more in thirty-four years. The five main host countries: United States (798,000), Dominican Republic (535,000), Chile (172,000), France (117,000), Canada (107,000). THIS IS NOT « THE DIASPORA »: the count is by place of BIRTH, never by descent — a child born in Brooklyn to Haitian parents is not in it, so the lived diaspora is larger, by an amount this source cannot estimate. NOR IS IT COMMUNE-LEVEL DATA, and it will not become so: no line says which commune the person left.
ds.prd038_h: Forced returns to Haiti — entry points and profile
ds.prd038_meta: 👥 Population • Sources : OIM/DTM avec l'ONM et le GARR — Suivi des retours forcés vers Haïti • confidence level B • Conditions OIM/DTM — publication sous réserve, passeport PSP-066
ds.prd038_p: 270,214 people were forcibly returned to Haiti in 2025, 36% more than in 2024, including 265,215 from the Dominican Republic (98%). They enter through points that ARE communes: Belladère receives 51% of arrivals, Ouanaminthe 27%. The first commune-level map on this subject. The profile follows: 66% adult men, but in a single year women rose 92%, girls 152% and boys 133%; average age 34; 85% had left for economic reasons; 32% hold no identity document; 19% were already displaced inside Haiti before leaving. ONLY TWO COMMUNES carry a share, and the other 138 are not at zero: they are without data.
ds.prd039_h: Removals from the United States — Haiti and the Dominican Republic
ds.prd039_meta: 👥 Population • Sources : DHS — Office of Homeland Security Statistics, Key Homeland Security Metrics : Repatriations • confidence level A • Domaine public — œuvre du gouvernement fédéral américain
ds.prd039_p: A MONTHLY series since October 2009, by country and by type of return — 364 observations. Long enough and regular enough to read a trend and a break. THE WORD « REPATRIATION » COVERS FOUR MECHANISMS: formal removal, enforcement return, administrative return, and Title 42 public-health expulsion. Adding them up under the word « deportation » inverts the reading: Haiti counts 14,090 repatriations in 2022, but only 1,540 formal removals — 12,360 were Title 42 expulsions, with no immigration proceeding. The comparison with the Dominican Republic is telling: before 2020 it had four to nine times more formal removals than Haiti; since 2023 it climbs back to 4,170 while Haiti stays at 740.
ds.prd040_h: Places of worship mapped, by commune
ds.prd040_meta: 📄 Société • Sources : OpenStreetMap via Overpass API • confidence level B • ODbL 1.0 — partage à l'identique
ds.prd040_p: 3,142 places of worship attached to 121 communes out of 140: 2,533 Christian, 279 VODOU, 12 spiritualist, 4 Muslim, and 302 with no religion tag. THIS IS NOT A CENSUS but the state of the MAPPING — a pale commune is far more likely one nobody has surveyed than one where few people worship. VODOU GETS ITS OWN COLUMN because no Haitian administrative register records it: folding it into a total would erase what is rare about this data. The 302 objects with no declared religion are not placed with the Christian ones — putting them there because « it is likely in Haiti » would replace an observation with an assumption.
ds.prd041_h: Licensed radio and television stations, by commune
ds.prd041_meta: 📄 Société • Sources : CONATEL — liste des stations de radiodiffusion autorisées 2023-2024 • confidence level A • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5
ds.prd041_p: 807 stations LICENSED by CONATEL: 665 FM radios, 8 AM radios and 134 television stations, with their frequency, owner and city. 80 communes hold at least one. THE OWNER IS PUBLISHED because a frequency is a conceded public good and the regulator publishes it itself. THE DOCUMENT CONTRADICTS ITSELF in three places — its headings announce 36 radios in Nippes, 20 television stations in Nord and 18 in Sud while its tables contain 35, 19 and 17 — and we publish what the tables contain, naming the gap.

jur.cgu_1h: What you may do, without asking anyone
jur.cgu_1p: Browse the Explorer, download the published files, reuse them in a dissertation, a report, an article, a map or a product — a commercial one included. No account, no e-mail, no need to warn us. The only obligation is to cite the source, and it comes from the licences, not from us.
jur.cgu_2h: The licences are not all the same
jur.cgu_2p: What Atmart produces — commune-level aggregates, recomputed indicators, comparisons between sources — is published under CC BY 4.0. But each source keeps its own, and some require more: share-alike for OpenStreetMap and OpenCelliD, no commercial use for ACLED. The register of sources gives, for each dataset, its licence and its two usage verdicts. That is where to look before reusing, not here.
jur.cgu_3h: What we ask you not to do
jur.cgu_4p: The data is supplied as is. We check it, we publish our controls and we write down its limits on every dataset — but we guarantee neither its accuracy, nor its completeness, nor its fitness for your use. A decision that commits people or funds should never rest on a single source, ours included. This is not a boilerplate clause: it is the very opposite of what we sell, which is the honest measure of what is not known.
jur.cgu_5p: The Explorer is free and will stay free. It carries no availability commitment. The published files are archived with their fingerprint, and the archives remain downloadable: that is our answer to an interruption, rather than a promise we could not keep.
jur.cgu_l1: Presenting a piece of data without its source, or without its vintage. A figure dated 2012 presented as current is no longer data, it is an assertion.
jur.cgu_l2: Replacing a missing value with a zero. Our files distinguish the two; confusing them changes the conclusions.
jur.cgu_l3: Pushing a national figure back down to the commune. Splitting a GDP across 140 communes manufactures 140 false values that carry the authority of a calculation.
jur.cgu_l4: Implying that Atmart approves your work, or is a co-author of it, merely because you use its data.
jur.cgu_l5: Querying our automated services at a rate that degrades the service for everyone else.
jur.con_p: We answer in French, Kreyòl, English and Spanish. Reporting an error is always welcome, including when it costs us: a false map corrected is worth more than a false map we are left free to publish.
jur.con_r4: Report a wrong figure or a badly cited source
jur.lead: Everything that binds Atmart to you, and you to Atmart. Written to be read: no pointing you to a document you cannot find, no clause whose meaning slips away. Where we do not have the information yet, we write that down rather than fill the gap.
jur.men_note: The three lines marked <mark class="jur-todo">to be completed</mark> legally bind Atmart: they will be filled in by Atmart, not guessed. An invented legal notice is worse than a missing one — an absence is seen, an invention is believed.
jur.men_pi_p: The Explorer's code, its layout, its methodological texts and its maps are the property of Atmart LLC. The data, on the other hand, is not: the aggregates produced by Atmart are under CC BY 4.0, and the original data stays under its producer's licence. In Haitian law, article 5 of the decree of 12 October 2005 excludes official administrative texts and “mere data” from protection — a fact belongs to no one, and we do not claim otherwise.
jur.sec_3h: What we cannot do, and why
jur.sec_3p: Two protections are missing, and they come down to the hosting: frame-ancestors, which prevents our pages from being embedded in a foreign frame, and HSTS on this subdomain. Both exist only as an HTTP header, and GitHub Pages does not let us customise them. We write it down rather than keep quiet about it: closing them would require a proxy in front of the site, which remains open to us.
jur.sec_4p: Write to security@atmart.ltd. Our policy is published in RFC 9116 format: /.well-known/security.txt. We acknowledge receipt within five working days and we credit you if you wish. We have no bounty programme — we say so rather than let anyone hope for one.
jur.sec_l1: A strict content security policy: no third-party script, every inline script authorised by its fingerprint, frames and objects forbidden, forms confined to the domain.
jur.sec_l2: Everything is served over HTTPS, and cleartext requests are rewritten to HTTPS.
jur.sec_l3: The referrer policy never passes the full page address to a third-party site.
jur.sec_l4: No address contains personal data: what you search for does not go into the address.
jur.sec_l5: The authorised origins are listed: a third-party page cannot query our services on a visitor's behalf.
jur.sec_l6: Form submissions are capped at five per address per day, the fields are truncated and their number is bounded.
jur.sec_l7: The access keys for third-party services stay server-side; none of them appears in the code sent to the browser.
jur.sec_l8: The assistant refuses to serve an answer containing a number absent from the page's data — the check is done server-side, after generation.
jur.sec_lead: We would rather describe our attack surface than pretend we have none. The Explorer is a static site: no account, no database, no content submitted by visitors. The risk therefore does not come from the page — it comes from the three things below.
jur.vie_1p: Thirteen aggregated counters, whose full list is published on the Trust & method page — we do not copy it out here, because two texts describing the same practice always end up diverging. Never collected: stored IP address, cookie, persistent identifier, browser fingerprint, and the text you type into the search box, which never leaves your browser.
jur.vie_2h: What you entrust to us voluntarily
jur.vie_2p: If you fill in a request form, the fields you type reach us by e-mail and are kept for one year to follow up your request. If you write to one of our addresses, your message is kept for as long as the relationship lasts. None of this is sold, rented, or passed to a third party for its own purposes.
jur.vie_4p: You can ask us what we hold about you, have it corrected, or have it erased: jeanmyril@atmart.ltd. We answer within thirty days. Since we keep almost nothing, the most frequent answer is “nothing, except the message you sent us” — and that is the point.
jur.vie_5h: The published data contains no personal data
jur.vie_5p: Everything the Explorer publishes is aggregated to the territory: a commune, a section, a department. No file names a person. The NGO register names organisations, not their members. This is a design rule, not a precaution: personal data does not enter the chain, and the control that verifies it blocks publication if it were to enter.

rz.en1_l1: Honest description — distributions, extreme values, missing data shown as missing, never quietly filled in
rz.en1_l2: Comparisons — means (t, Welch), proportions (chi-square, Fisher exact), ranks (Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis), analysis of variance
rz.en1_l3: Multiple testing — Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg correction as soon as several hypotheses are tested on the same data, otherwise you end up “finding” pure chance
rz.en1_l4: Always three numbers — the effect size in its real unit, its confidence interval, and only then the p-value
rz.en2_l1: The model follows the variable — continuous: linear regression; binary: logistic (odds ratios and marginal effects); counts: Poisson or negative binomial; repeated observations: fixed or random effects
rz.en2_l2: Robust standard errors by default — HC0 to HC3, or clustered by branch, region or individual when observations are not independent
rz.en2_l3: Automatic diagnostics — heteroskedasticity (Breusch-Pagan, White), autocorrelation (Durbin-Watson), collinearity (VIF), functional form (RESET), residual normality (Jarque-Bera) — each warning comes with its remedy
rz.en2_l4: Causal designs — difference-in-differences, instrumental variables (2SLS, with a weak-instrument warning), panel fixed effects
rz.en3_l1: Time series — trend, seasonality, breaks, ARIMA and exponential smoothing, validated on a period held back
rz.en3_l2: Bayesian forecasting — the output is not a number but a distribution: you read the interval, not just the central point
rz.en3_l3: Updating — each new period tightens the forecast instead of recomputing everything from scratch
rz.en3_l4: Hierarchical models — a branch, area or batch with few observations borrows information from the others, instead of producing a wild estimate from three cases
rz.en4_l1: No result without its diagnostic — convergence, effective sample size, divergences, predictive checks: a result that fails its controls does not go into a report
rz.en4_l2: Sensitivity — what the conclusion becomes if you change the starting assumption, the period kept or the cases excluded
rz.en4_l3: Reproducible — every result can be replayed: the data at the time of computation, the method, the version, the person who validated it
rz.en4_l4: Readable without being a statistician — every output comes with a plain sentence saying what the figure means, and what it does not say
rz.en_d: Four families of questions, four families of methods. The tool picks, with you, the one that matches your question and the shape of your data — and rules out the one that does not.
rz.en_rule: ⚖️ The rule written into the tool: a result is called an effect only if a design is named and its key assumption stated. Everywhere else, the report says association. A coefficient is not causal because it comes from a regression — it is causal thanks to the design around it. That is the whole difference between a dashboard that impresses and a figure that holds up in front of an auditor, a credit committee or a peer reviewer.
rz.en_warn: ⚠️ What we do not promise. Rezilta replaces neither the regulatory validation of a banking risk model, nor an accredited laboratory system, nor an ethics committee. It supplies what those procedures demand and what is almost always missing: the audit trail, the written method, the diagnostics and reproducibility. The decision remains yours.
rz.end_d: The pilot programme is open to a few organisations. You bring a project in progress, we bring the tool and the method — and you keep everything that is produced.
rz.end_t: Let us build it on your real project

rz.fq1_a: A project management tool tracks tasks. Rezilta tracks results: it links the activity to the indicator, the indicator to its source, and the source to the report. That is the chain an audit demands and that no spreadsheet holds over time.
rz.fq1_q: How is this different from a spreadsheet or a project management tool?
rz.fq2_a: No. Rezilta generates your forms towards Kobo/XLSForm, and everything comes out as Excel, PDF or a Power BI template. The aim is to connect what you already use, not to force you to replace it.
rz.fq2_q: Do we have to abandon Kobo, Excel or Power BI?
rz.fq3_a: Minimisation principle: we only collect what serves an indicator. Personal data is kept separate from analysis data, access is partitioned by team, and nothing is resold or used to train a model. A written agreement frames every processing operation.
rz.fq4_a: Formation360 remains available for producing sessions and training materials. Rezilta takes over and widens the project side — design, indicators, evaluation, reports — for any type of activity, not just training.
rz.fq5_a: Never. It proposes an analysis, a first draft of a narrative, an anomaly detection — every proposal is identified as such, and a person validates before it enters a report. Responsibility stays human.
rz.fq6_a: Yes. The Project module is an option, not the core. A bank, a laboratory or a sales department uses the three layers — foundation, analysis, delivery — without ever opening a logical framework.
rz.fq6_q: We do not run projects, only data. Is this for us?
rz.fq7_a: No. You ask the question, the tool proposes the method that matches your data and translates the result into plain language. But the script and the data are always available: anyone who wants to check, or redo the computation in R, can do so at any time.
rz.fq7_q: Do you need to code or to be a statistician?
rz.fq8_a: Not on its word — which is why every result arrives with its diagnostics, its written assumptions and its script. A conclusion that fails its controls is flagged, not dressed up. And when the data does not allow a conclusion, the tool is built to say so rather than produce a reassuring figure.

sx.fil: Does tutoring improve success, or does it already attract the strongest?
sx.lead: You have tracked cohorts for years. The question is not counting — it is knowing whether the gap between two groups comes from the scheme or from who signs up for it. Rezilta refuses to confuse the two.
sx.li: Rezilta is not a student records system: it handles no enrolments, no grades, no timetables. It judges no teacher and produces no institutional ranking. On student data it applies the same minimisation as everywhere else: only what serves a question is collected, and identity stays separate from analysis.
sx.q1_d: The tool does not decide for you: it requires you to name the design that would prove it, and writes “association” until you have.
sx.q1_t: Does the scheme work, or does it select?
sx.q2_d: Breakdown by sex, age, geographic origin, programme. That is where what an overall rate hides becomes visible.
sx.q3_d: Comparison across years on the same definitions. Without stable definitions, a difference in rates means nothing.
sx.re1: Cohorts tracked on the same definitions from one year to the next
sx.re2: Measured gaps, with selection flagged where it exists
sx.re3: An explicit line between an observed link and an effect
sx.re4: A result your students can reproduce — the script comes with it
sx.sc_1: Students who took the tutoring pass at 78 %, the others at 61 %. The conclusion drops: tutoring works, let us extend it. Nobody notices that tutoring is optional — and that those who sign up are precisely the ones already working hardest.
sx.sc_2: With Rezilta, the gap is measured properly, with its interval. But until someone names a design and writes down why it holds, the result is recorded as an association: “tutored students pass more often” — which is true — and not “tutoring improves success”, which is not, yet.

xp.box_h3: What this explorer does — and what it does not
xp.box_p1: It shows the information currently documented by Atmart Data — not everything that exists about a commune. Everything runs in your browser: four public files and one map outline, no application server, no account, no advertising tracker. An anonymous and aggregated audience measurement counts uses (a search happened) without ever knowing who or what — no cookie, no identifier, no IP address kept, and the text you type never leaves your browser: full method. What you see, you can download as is from the catalogue and recompute yourself.
